privacy.controlsBody: Clear search history from Library → Searches. Erase everything, or export a JSON copy, from Settings. Removing a library entry never deletes a file that was already saved to your device.
privacy.cookiesBody: No cookies, no third-party analytics, no advertising identifiers. The only persistent browser values are the two install flags described above, and they never leave your device.
privacy.copyrightBody: Only files a provider publishes for download are saved: catalogue preview clips and hosts an operator has explicitly put on the authorized list. YouTube videos are streamed through the official player and are never downloaded or extracted. Nothing here circumvents DRM, paywalls, access controls or platform terms. If a provider does not offer a file, the app says so instead of showing a button that cannot work.
privacy.headline: Your data, on your device.
privacy.sent.audioBody: Audio samples are produced only while you are identifying: a 16 kHz mono WAV is posted to this app’s server, forwarded to ACRCloud, and returned — it is not written to disk and is not retained after the request. Search terms go from the server to the provider; your API keys stay on the server and never reach the browser.
privacy.sent.countsBody: A successful identification also increments a counter for that track (title, artist, day). It is an aggregate — no account, no device id, no address, and no link between you and the track — and it exists only so trending can show what this app’s users actually identify.
